items.title: Inflation jumps to 4.9% as fuel prices surge, but the RBA should hold rates steady
paras: Darren England/AAP Inflation jumps to 4.9% as fuel prices surge, but the RBA should hold rates steady Published: November 24, 2026 9:46pm EST Annual headline inflation jumped to 4.9% in October, up from 4.3% in September, driven by a spike in petrol and diesel prices as global oil prices surged.

Today’s release from the Australian Bureau of Statistics also shows underlying inflation, measured by the “ trimmed mean ”, rose to an annual rate of 3.8%. This is the Reserve Bank of Australia’s (RBA) preferred measure of underlying inflation, as it removes the influence of unusually large price movements.

Both measures were above market forecasts, and remain well above the RBA’s target range of 2–3%. This is despite five interest rate increases this year that have lifted the cash rate from 3.60% to 4.85%.

While the latest inflation figures are concerning, they need to be interpreted in the context of a rapidly weakening labour market. The economic landscape has changed considerably since the RBA last raised interest rates early this month.
The RBA has two key objectives : maintaining price stability and achieving full employment. Balancing these goals is becoming increasingly difficult.
Last week’s jobs report showed Australia’s unemployment rate rose to 4.9% in October, its highest level since October 2021. The number of unemployed Australians increased by 17,800 to 753,700.

Notably, the October unemployment rate has already reached 4.9%, a level the RBA, in its November Statement on Monetary Policy , projected for the December quarter of 2027. This suggests the labour market is weakening considerably faster than the RBA anticipated.
The sharp deterioration in the jobs market over the past two months suggests the cumulative effects of previous interest rate increases are starting to bite.

Higher interest rates increase mortgage repayments, leaving many households with less money to spend. Businesses facing weaker consumer demand and higher borrowing costs are likely to scale back investment and recruitment.
These are precisely the channels through which the RBA’s monetary policy works to bring inflation down .
However, the speed at which the jobs market is deteriorating raises concerns that interest rates may have risen too far.
Further rate hikes might help bring inflation down more quickly, but potentially at a considerable cost in terms of lost jobs and weaker economic growth.
One encouraging development since the RBA’s November meeting has been the decline in global oil prices, which were a key driver of the rise in inflation in October.
Brent crude oil is currently trading at around US$91 a barrel, well below its US$125 peak last month.

First, cheaper petrol directly reduces headline inflation, as automotive fuel is a component of the transport group in the consumer price index. It also provides some immediate cost-of-living relief for households.

Second, lower fuel prices reduce transport, production and distribution costs for businesses. Over time, some of these cost savings may be passed on to consumers through lower prices for other goods and services.
While the direct impact on headline inflation can occur relatively quickly, the broader effects on underlying inflation will take longer to materialise.
Importantly, lower oil prices could help bring inflation down without the need for further interest rate increases or further weakness in the labour market.
The RBA will hold its final monetary policy meeting of the year on December 8. Despite today’s elevated inflation figures, I expect the RBA to leave the cash rate unchanged at 4.85%.
Financial markets appear to share this view, pricing in a 80% probability of the RBA holding rates steady in December .
Following last week’s weaker labour market figures, expectations have shifted towards rate cuts, with some major banks anticipating the first cut as early as June 2027 .
This is a remarkable shift in expectations, given that the RBA raised interest rates just three weeks ago and inflation remains well above target.
It suggests the balance of risks is shifting, with concerns about rising unemployment and slowing economic growth becoming increasingly important in shaping expectations about the next move in rates.
Throughout this year, the RBA has understandably prioritised bringing inflation under control.
However, recent developments raise the question of whether it has placed too much weight on inflation while underestimating weakness in the labour market.

Monetary policy operates with what economists call long and variable lags . Interest rate increases can take many months to fully flow through to household spending, business investment, employment and inflation. The Australian economy has therefore yet to absorb the full effects of this year’s five rate hikes.
Further rate rises risk pushing the economy too far. By the time inflation returns to target, unemployment could be considerably higher and recession risks greater.
The RBA needs to be forward-looking, considering where both inflation and unemployment are likely to be in 12 to 18 months.
Given the weakening labour market and falling oil prices, holding interest rates steady would give the central bank more time to assess the impact of its previous decisions.
The RBA has spent much of this year fighting inflation. It now needs to ensure that winning that fight does not come at an unnecessarily high cost to Australian jobs.

items.title: Worse than expected inflation keeps pressure on rates
paras: The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) has released CPI inflation data for October, which came in stronger than expected.

Annual headline inflation jumped to 4.9%, whereas the policy-relevant trimmed mean inflation rose to 3.8% – both well above economists’ expectations and the Reserve Bank of Australia’s (RBA) inflation target of 2% to 3%:
The result challenges the view that October would mark the peak in inflation. The RBA’s own November forecasts had headline inflation topping out at 4.5%.
“Non-discretionary items (~60% of the basket) up over 6% through the year”, Alex Joiner, chief economist at IFM Investors, wrote on X (Twitter).
“The domestic inflation problem continues, and the risk is that the RBA is put in the worst of situations with inflation persisting at an elevated rate while the unemployment rate moves higher”.
The following chart from Joiner plots trimmed mean inflation against the RBA’s November Statement of Monetary Policy (SoMP) forecasts:
“This will need to be the peak in trimmed mean inflation for the RBA’s conservative forecasts to be met”, Joiner wrote.
With unemployment also tracking well above the RBA’s forecast, Australia is facing a stagflationary environment of falling per capita growth, rising unemployment and rising inflation.
This is a central banker’s nightmare, as well as a nightmare for indebted Australians, who face a rising repayment burden and a precarious jobs market.

items.title: Inflation rises more than expected in 'RBA's worst nightmare'
paras: The Reserve Bank forecasts inflation to remain outside of its target band for another year. ( ABC Pilbara: Cody Fenner )
The consumer price index lifted more than forecast in October, with inflation and unemployment now above the Reserve Bank's forecasts.
Housing was the largest contributor to annual inflation, driven by electricity and new dwelling prices, as builders passed on higher costs.
The RBA board next meets in just under a fortnight's time, with its interest rates decision to be handed down on December 8.
Inflation has come in hotter than expected in October, leaving Australia grappling with accelerating price rises and increasing unemployment.
The consumer price index rose half a per cent in October, in original terms, with the annual rate of inflation lifting to 4.9 per cent, the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) said.

The trimmed mean, a measure of underlying inflation, also picked up pace, rising 3.8 per cent over the year. Economists had expected it to remain steady at 3.6 per cent, which would have still been above the Reserve Bank's target of 2-3 per cent.
The RBA had forecast headline inflation to remain elevated for another year, before easing to 2.7 per cent by the end of 2027.
However, headline inflation, underlying inflation and unemployment are now all above where the central bank had forecast them to sit at the end of 2026.
"Rising inflation and unemployment are the RBA's worst nightmare," Oxford Economics head of economic research Harry Murphy Cruise said.

"Both are at odds with its dual mandate of price stability and full employment, but they require opposing policy responses. Taming inflation requires higher rates, but that comes at the expense of employment."
The RBA board next meets in just under a fortnight's time, with its interest rates decision to be handed down on December 8.
Betashares chief economist David Bassanese said the higher-than-expected underlying inflation result highlighted the "tough challenge" facing the economy.
"Although economic growth has slowed, the inflation dragon has not yet been slain," Mr Bassanese wrote.
Mr Bassanese, who has been forecasting a February rate hike, said it "remain[ed] on the table".
"Overall, while the economy is showing signs of slowing, the risk is that it has not slowed enough. If the RBA moves rates in 2027, the risk remains tilted towards a hike."
Oxford Economics has maintained its view that rates will remain on hold in December and through 2027.
Economists at UBS, on the other hand, still expect the RBA to cut interest rates in August 2027.

While they saw the high inflation numbers as raising the risk of an extra rate hike in February, they noted that the split in the central bank board, with "dovish external board members" arguing for rates to remain on hold, would likely mean no hike.
Housing was the largest contributor to annual inflation in October, the ABS said. Housing prices rose 6.4 per cent, compared to a rise of 5.2 per cent in the 12 months to September.
Electricity, which is classified as a housing cost, rose 25.2 per cent over the year to October.

"The rise in electricity reflects Commonwealth government rebates, which reduced household electricity costs last year but are no longer in place," ABS head of price statistics Rachael McCririck said.
New dwelling prices also increased in pace, up 5.1 per cent annually, driven by builders passing on higher costs for materials and labour.
Transport was the second biggest contributor due to rising automotive fuel prices.
Fuel was excluded from the trimmed mean in October, and this was a key driver of the difference between headline and trimmed mean inflation, the ABS said.

items.title: ASX widens losses after inflation shock; Harvey Norman plunges
paras: Advertisement Updated Business Markets World markets ASX widens losses after inflation shock; Harvey Norman plunges Staff writers Updated November 25, 2026 — 10:56am , first published 5:26am
You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month.

Share A A A The Australian sharemarket was already feeling a hangover from Tuesday’s Nvidia rally, but extended its losses after figures showed annual inflation has soared to its highest level since the start of the war against Iran, raising concerns about the strength of the Australian economy.

The S&P/ASX 200 fell 67.40 points, or 0.8 per cent, to 8659 at around 11.45am AEDT, widening its early losses. The local bourse had opened lower after the tech relief rally over Jensen Huang’s return to the helm of Nvidia fizzled on Wall Street overnight. The ASX surged 1.8 per cent on Tuesday.

AI stocks weighed down Wall Street on Tuesday after Monday’s Nvidia-driven surge. Bloomberg The Australian dollar rose to US66.53¢. The Australian Bureau of Statistics said annual inflation hit 4.9 per cent in October, up from 4.3 per cent in September. Of concern for the Reserve Bank, the measure of underlying inflation lifted by 0.5 per cent to 3.8 per cent.

That’s still well above the RBA’s target range of 2 to 3 per cent, despite five rate hikes to reign in inflation this year. However, with unemployment at a five-year-high, markets have started to price in rate cuts next year aimed to prop up the economy.

Harvey Norman shares plunged 4.7 per cent after the furniture seller warned its profits since the start of the financial year were down by almost half as shoppers closed their wallets in the cost-of-living crisis. Unaudited profit before tax from July 1 to October 31 was down 47 per cent, the retailer said, though the Black Friday and Christmas sales yet to come usually generate a large share of half-year profits. Its rivals Nick Scali and Temple & Webster lost 1.8 per cent and 2.7 per cent.

Meanwhile, the materials sector led losses on the ASX, with BHP and Rio Tinto down 2.9 per cent and 2 per cent. Copper, their main earnings driver, closed at a 13-month low as a selloff in the US tech giants refuelled concerns about future demand for the red metal, which provides the wiring for the AI sector.

Gold also fell, pushing gold producers Northern Star (down 2.5 per cent), Evolution Mining (down 2.4 per cent) and Newmont (down 1.5 per cent) lower. The precious metal erased most of Monday’s dramatic rebound after a report that the US was preparing to announce plans to raise levies on imported good weighed on equities, and as investors contemplated further interest rate hikes in the world’s largest economy. Higher rates are a headwind for gold, which doesn’t yield any interest.

AI-related tech stocks NextDC and Megaport traded lower, down 2.2 per cent and 7 per cent, following the sector’s sell-off in the US. Software maker WiseTech, Australia’s biggest tech stock, wiped out early gains to trade down 0.6 per cent.
The Big Four banks swung into the red following the inflation data. CBA and National Australia Bank were down 1 per cent, Westpac dropped 1.4 per cent and ANZ Bank slipped 0.8 per cent.

Energy stocks benefited from a rise in the oil price, which edged higher in thin trading as reports of further tanker attacks overshadowed the latest diplomatic efforts to resolve the US-Iran war. Brent crude was up 2.3 per cent at $US91.40 a barrel. Local oil giants Woodside and Santos rose 2.9 per cent and 2.2 per cent, respectively, limiting the wider market’s losses.

On Wall Street overnight, the S&P 500 fell 0.5 per cent to its eighth loss in the last nine days. Tech stocks once again led the way and yanked the Nasdaq composite down a market-leading 1.5 per cent. Stocks outside of AI held up much better, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.9 per cent.

Wall Street’s swings are the latest for a market that’s been mostly sinking since hitting its all-time high last month. The worry is that prices for AI-related stocks shot too high into a possible bubble and need to deflate. That carries immense consequences for the broader market and workers’ retirement accounts because AI companies have grown into Wall Street’s most influential stocks.

While the surprise return of Jensen Huang as Nvidia’s CEO announced does bring back a charismatic leader who championed and helped build the entire AI industry, it does not settle the deep concerns dogging it. For one, doubts remain about whether AI can possibly produce enough profit and productivity to make the massive investments underway in data centres worth it.

At the same time, high interest rates make it more difficult to borrow money to pay for the industry’s growth. Sweeping victories for Democrats earlier this month in the US midterm elections, meanwhile, have raised concerns about more regulation for AI, including possible halts to further construction of data centres.
To be sure, AI stocks and the broader US market have been prone to extreme reversals since the summer, not only week to week but even hour to hour.
Nvidia fell 5.9 per cent a day after soaring 31.5 per cent to its biggest gain in more than two decades. Other stocks around the AI industry fell by similar amounts.
CoreWeave, which buys Nvidia chips and rents out access to them over the cloud, tumbled 11.8 per cent. GE Vernova, which is helping to power AI data centres, dropped 4.8 per cent.

And Anthropic, the company behind the Claude AI chatbot, sank 6.5 per cent to drop below $US83. That’s how much Anthropic first sold its stock for in its initial public offering last week. The stock had briefly jumped as high as $US115 in its first day of trading amid a frenzy of hype.

Such drops were powerful enough to drag the S&P 500 index lower even though most of the stocks within the index climbed. They rose following the latest report to say confidence among US consumers is improving by more than economists expected.
Companies in industries across the US economy, meanwhile, continue to report strong growth in profits for the summer.

Dollar Tree climbed 11.2 per cent after reporting bigger earnings for the latest quarter than analysts expected. The average shopper spent slightly more in its stores during the three months than they did in last year’s third quarter, and more of them came in than last year.

Kohl’s rallied 19.5 per cent after reporting a profit for the latest quarter, when analysts were expecting basically zero. It also gave forecasts for revenue for the final three months of its fiscal year that were better than expected.
In the bond market, Treasury yields held relatively steady. The yield on the 10-year Treasury rose to 4.93 per cent from 4.92 per cent late on Monday after drifting up and down earlier in the day.

items.title: Financial market pivots to rate cuts
paras: Recent RBA communications have suggested that the labour market remains “a little tight”. However, last week’s labour force release from the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) challenged that view, suggesting the job market is in balance and could soon move into oversupply.

Other recent indicators also suggest that the economy is deteriorating, including the record downturn in the property market (both prices and transaction volumes), surveyed business conditions tracking negative in the past three months, business and consumer confidence falling to historically low levels and forward orders weakening sharply.

items.title: RBI releases 2026 list of Domestic Systemically Important Banks (D-SIBs)
paras: State Bank of India, HDFC Bank, and ICICI Bank continue to be identified as Domestic Systemically Important Banks (D-SIBs) under the same bucketing structure as in the 2025 list of D-SIBs . The additional Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) requirement for these D-SIBs will be in addition to the capital conservation buffer. The list of D-SIBs is as follows: Bucket Banks Additional Common Equity Tier 1 requirement as a percentage of Risk Weighted Assets (RWAs) 5 - 1% 4 State Bank of India 0.80% 3 - 0.60% 2 HDFC Bank 0.40% 1 ICICI Bank 0.20% Background: The Reserve Bank had issued the Framework for dealing with Domestic Systemically Important Banks (D-SIBs) on July 22, 2014 , which was subsequently updated on December 28, 2023 . The D-SIB framework requires the Reserve Bank to disclose the names of banks designated as D-SIBs starting from 2015 and place these banks in appropriate buckets depending upon their Systemic Importance Scores (SISs). Based on the bucket in which a D-SIB is placed, an additional common equity requirement has to be applied to it. In case a foreign bank having branch presence in India is a Global Systemically Important Bank (G-SIB) , it has to maintain additional CET1 capital surcharge in India as applicable to it as a G-SIB, proportionate to its Risk Weighted Assets (RWAs) in India, i.e., additional CET1 buffer prescribed by the home regulator (amount) multiplied by India RWA as per consolidated global Group books divided by total consolidated global Group RWA. The Reserve Bank had announced SBI and ICICI Bank as D-SIBs in 2015 and 2016 while HDFC Bank was classified as D-SIB in 2017 along with SBI and ICICI Bank. The current update is based on the data collected from banks as on March 31, 2026. (Brij Raj) Chief General Manager Press Release: 2026-2027/1547

items.title: RBI issues Draft Amendment Directions for ‘Preventive Safeguards for Electronic Banking Transactions (EBTs)’
paras: The Reserve Bank had issued the Amendment Directions dated June 24, 2026 on ‘ Customer Protection in Fraudulent Electronic Banking Transactions ’ which, inter alia, strengthened the existing framework for limiting liability of customers in unauthorised Electronic Banking Transactions (EBTs). While the revised framework primarily addresses customer liability in the event of fraudulent EBTs, a need is felt to strengthen the same from a preventive perspective by providing customers with greater control over the manner and extent to which digital payment channels may be used. Further, on a review to bring in uniformity in practices adopted by banks and ensure that customers are protected against specific acts of omission or commission on part of the banks, it has been decided to expand the scope of the definition of ‘negligence by a bank’ specified in the aforementioned Amendment Directions. 2. Accordingly, the Reserve Bank has today issued the following draft Amendment Directions for public comments, which propose to amend Directions on Responsible Business Conduct issued by the Department of Regulation, RBI: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks - Responsible Business Conduct) Fifth Amendment Directions, 2026 Reserve Bank of India (Small Finance Banks - Responsible Business Conduct) Fifth Amendment Directions, 2026 Reserve Bank of India (Payments Banks - Responsible Business Conduct) Third Amendment Directions, 2026 Reserve Bank of India (Local Area Banks - Responsible Business Conduct) Fifth Amendment Directions, 2026 Reserve Bank of India (Regional Rural Banks - Responsible Business Conduct) Fifth Amendment Directions, 2026 Reserve Bank of India (Urban Co-operative Banks - Responsible Business Conduct) Fifth Amendment Directions, 2026 Reserve Bank of India (Rural Co-operative Banks - Responsible Business Conduct) Fifth Amendment Directions, 2026 3. The comments / feedback on the draft Amendment Directions may be submitted by the regulated entities and members of public / other stakeholders on or before December 14, 2026 through the following channels: the ‘ Connect 2 Regulate ’ section on the website by following the corresponding hyperlink provided against each document in the page where they are hosted; or by email with the subject line ‘Feedback on (full name of the draft Amendment Directions (including the type of Regulated Entity))’. (Brij Raj) Chief General Manager Press Release: 2026-2027/1548

items.title: Governor, Reserve Bank of India meets Managing Directors & Chief Executive Officers of select NBFCs, HFCs and Industry R
paras: As part of the Reserve Bank’s ongoing engagement with regulated entities, the Governor, Reserve Bank of India, today met in Mumbai with the Managing Directors and Chief Executive Officers (MDs & CEOs) of select Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs), including Government NBFCs, Housing Finance Companies (HFCs) and Microfinance Institutions. Representatives of Sa-Dhan, the Micro Finance Institutions Network (MFIN) and the Finance Industry Development Council (FIDC) also participated. Deputy Governors Shri Swaminathan J., Dr Poonam Gupta, Shri S. C. Murmu and Shri Rohit Jain attended the meeting, along with other senior officers of the Reserve Bank. The MD & CEO of the National Housing Bank also participated. The Governor acknowledged the role of NBFCs and HFCs in supporting economic activity by widening access to credit. He emphasised the need for responsible and sustainable credit growth and urged NBFCs to put customers first as they expand their business. He highlighted the importance of quality service, effective grievance redressal and fair recovery practices. He also encouraged NBFCs to use the Central KYC Records Registry (CKYCR) for customer onboarding and to keep customer records in the registry up to date to improve customer convenience. The Governor urged participants to strengthen their cybersecurity infrastructure and adopt a comprehensive, risk-based approach to managing cyber and IT risks, with appropriate oversight by their boards and senior management. Participants shared feedback on policy and operational matters concerning the NBFC sector. (Brij Raj) Chief General Manager Press Release: 2026-2027/1554

items.title: Reserve Bank (Securitisation Transactions) Amendment Directions, 2026
paras: The Reserve Bank of India had, on July 27, 2026 , issued the Draft (Securitisation Transactions) Amendment Directions for stakeholder feedback. 2. A statement on the feedback received on the draft Directions is provided in the Annex . 3. Accordingly, the Reserve Bank has today issued the final Amendment Directions as given below: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Securitisation Transactions) Amendment Directions, 2026 Reserve Bank of India (Small Finance Banks – Securitisation Transactions) Amendment Directions, 2026 Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Securitisation Transactions) Amendment Directions, 2026 Reserve Bank of India (All India Financial Institutions – Securitisation Transactions) Amendment Directions, 2026 5. The guidelines will come into force from April 01, 2027. (Brij Raj) Chief General Manager Press Release: 2026-2027/1550

items.title: Indian students in Kazan delighted as PM Modi arrives for BRICS Summit
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel Kazan [ Russia ], October 22 (ANI): Indian students in Kazan , Russia , are happy and excited about Prime Minister Narendra Modi's arrival at Hotel Korston , as he attends the 16th BRICS Summit . Notably, PM Narendra Modi on Tuesday touched down in Kazan city of Russia to participate in the 16th BRICS Summit and received a warm welcome. He is here to attend the 16th BRICS Summit , being held under the Chairmanship of Russia . To welcome PM Modi , students from India studying in Russia also sang a welcome song as they awaited PM Modi 's arrival at Hotel Korston . An Indian student from Pune, Saniya said that the students are quite excited to greet PM Modi . "Maybe we will get the opportunity (to meet PM Modi ) as many students are here (at Hotel Korston )... We are very excited. We are lucky to have this opportunity and we are happy to see him," she told ANI. An Indian student from Bihar, Shaurya Pratap said, "We are very happy to welcome PM Modi and we have prepared a song for him and we hope he likes it." Surbhi from Delhi said, "I have been here in Kazan since 2019 and today, we are going to sing a song for PM Modi and we are very excited about that." Parul, a final-year medical student, who has been in Kazan for the last five years told ANI, "We are really grateful that we got this opportunity to welcome our dear Prime Minister." Arti Pawar from Maharashtra said, "I have been living here for the past three years. I am very happy that PM Modi is coming here." Mrunmayi from Nagpur, Maharashtra said, "All the students here are quite enthusiastic as PM is going to come soon. We are too much delighted to welcome him." Meanwhile, ISKCON volunteers - from the Russia n and Indian communities were seen chanting 'Hare Krishna, Hare Ram' ahead of PM Modi 's arrival. While speaking with ANI, Sergoy, an ISKCON volunteer, said, "'Hare Krishna is a Mahamantra. This visit of PM Modi to Kazan , Russia is an important one for us. We are happy." Another ISKCON volunteer said, "We want to welcome PM Modi here in Kazan . It's a great honour for us to welcome him here We are very excited to see him." A Russia n citizen, Alexander said that the people there will welcome PM Modi by singing a song and that he is happy with PM Modi 's visit to Kazan . He said, "We have made a banner and we will also sing a song to welcome PM Modi ... I returned from India just two days back and directly came from Delhi to Kazan to see PM Modi . I am very happy that he is coming to Russia ." Notably, ahead of his departure to Russia , PM Modi shared a post on X and wrote, "Leaving for Kazan , Russia , to take part in the BRICS Summit . India attaches immense importance to BRICS, and I look forward to extensive discussions on a wide range of subjects. I also look forward to meeting various leaders there." The Prime Minister's office in a statement quoted PM Modi as saying, "I am departing today on a two-day visit to Kazan at the invitation of H.E. Mr. Vladimir Putin, President of the Russia n Federation, to attend the 16th BRICS Summit ." "India values the close cooperation within BRICS which has emerged as an important platform for dialogue and discussion on issues concerning the global developmental agenda, reformed multilateralism, climate change, economic cooperation, building resilient supply chains, promoting cultural and people to people connect, among others," PM Modi said. The statement further said that the expansion of BRICS with the addition of new members last year has added to its inclusivity and agenda for the global good. "Building upon the Annual Summit held in July 2024 in Moscow, my visit to Kazan will further reinforce the Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership between India and Russia . I look forward to meeting other leaders from BRICS as well," the PMO statement said. The 16th BRICS Summit in Kazan is being held under the chairmanship of Russia from October 22-24. During his visit, PM Modi is also expected to hold bilateral meetings with his counterparts from BRICS member countries and invited leaders in Kazan . The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said, "The Summit, themed 'Strengthening Multilateralism for Just Global Development and Security,' will provide an important platform for leaders to discuss key global issues." It further said, "The Summit will offer a valuable opportunity to assess the progress of initiatives launched by BRICS and to identify potential areas for future collaboration." This visit marks, PM Modi 's second visit to Russia this year. He travelled to Moscow in July to attend the 22nd India- Russia Annual Summit where he held a bilateral meeting with President Putin. He was also conferred with Russia 's highest civilian award, the Order of St. Andrew the Apostle at the Kremlin in Moscow. BRIC, as a formal grouping, started after the meeting of the Leaders of Russia , India and China in St Petersburg on the margins of G8 Outreach Summit in 2006. The grouping was formalized during the first meeting of BRIC Foreign Ministers on the margins of UNGA in New York in 2006. The first BRIC Summit was held in Russia 's Yekaterinburg in 2009. It was agreed to expand BRIC into BRICS with the inclusion of South Africa at the BRIC Foreign Ministers' meeting in New York in 2010. South Africa attended the 3rd BRICS Summit in Sanya in 2011. A further expansion of BRICS took place in 2024 with five new members - Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, Saudi Arabia, and the United Arab Emirates. (ANI)

items.title: "Singapore plays key role in Act-East policy": Rajnath Singh at India-Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [ India ], October 22 (ANI): Dr. Ng Eng Hen , Singapore 's Minister of Defence , has begun his three-day visit to India . As part of his visit, Dr. Hen co-chaired the sixth India - Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue in New Delhi, with his India n counterpart Rajnath Singh . The Summit began on Tuesday morning, with India n Defence Minister Rajnath Singh welcoming the Singapore delegation warmly. He noted that the strategic partnership the two countries share is a "testimony of increasing closeness between our countries." Singh said, " The meeting is happening at a time when India marks the decade of India 's Act in Policy, in which Singapore has played a key role in promoting economic cooperation, cultural ties, and developed strategic connectivity with country institutions." Building upon Singh's remarks, Dr. Ng Eng Hen said, "You reminded us that this is the 10th year since your Act East Policy. From Singapore 's perspective, India has always been part of the East. Whether you choose to act or look, we consider you part of the area." He said that while remembering the history of Singapore , India has been an important partner. " When we started the Singapore armed forces, one of the countries that we asked early on to see whether they could help us was India ." Hen highlighted that such historical memoirs serve as important reminders and "reflects how we feel that India is very part of our area. We are delighted that our ten years of bilateral relations have been very much improved in defence and all-round strategic partnership." Hen also thanked PM Modi for visiting Singapore earlier this year and noted that the visit was an excellent meeting. A day before, the Ministry of Defence had announced the sixth India - Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue in New Delhi on October 22, 2024. The release noted that between India and Singapore , "The engagements have diversified to include wide-ranging contacts between the Services, military-to-military exchanges, high-level visits, capacity building and training programs, cooperation in UN Peacekeeping, ship visits and bilateral exercises." Inaugurated in 2016, the India - Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue is a key platform to strengthen bilateral defence cooperation between Singapore and India . The fifth edition of the Defence Ministers' Dialogue took place in January 2021 through virtual teleconference. During the meeting, the two parties showed confidence in the outcomes of the meeting that would result in providing impetus to the entire spectrum of the bilateral engagement as well as to the regional security architecture. (ANI)

items.title: "India matters most for future of planet" says British High Commissioner Lindy Cameron
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): In recent times when climate change has become a pressing issue with countries across the world being ravaged due to climate catastrophes, it becomes imperative to discuss and deliberate upon global actions that can help the world rise up and meet these challenges. At the NDTV World Summit's a discussion was held on the theme, "India Matters The Most For Future Of Planet". Participants in the discussion included Erik Solheim, Former Minister of Climate and the Environment of Norway; Lindy Cameron , British High Commissioner to India; Shishir Priyadarshi, President Chintan Research Foundation; Harjeet Singh, Global Engagement Director, Fossil Fuel Non-Proliferation Treaty Initiative. "India is the country that matters the most for the future of the planet and climate change. India's ambition for development should not in any way be constrained by the responsibilities of the planet," Lindy Cameron , British High Commissioner to India, emphasised. She noted that the UK is committed towards the Multilateral Development Banks (MDB) reforms, technology and research support in India to aid the efforts. "Every dollar invested in resilient infrastructure pays 4 times over," said Cameron. "Lived experience of climate emergencies helps people to understand why their government needs to take policy action now," she added. Further talking about the need for urgent government action, Harjeet Singh, Global Engagement Director, Fossil Fuel Non-Proliferation Treaty Initiative said, "Series of disasters affecting both developed and developing countries are serving as a wake-up call. As rich countries will get more and more affected by climate change which they did not imagine till a couple of years ago, most vulnerable countries are going to be struggling with impacts who also have very less capacity to deal with it. India is taking a leadership role in the global fight against climate change. Initiatives such as Global Biofuels Alliance, International Solar Alliance, and Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure are some efforts taken by India in recent years to manage the climate crisis. (ANI)

items.title: Asia's Largest Mindfulness India Summit 2024 Marks a New Era for Corporate Culture and Personal Well-being with the Inau
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel PNN Mumbai (Maharashtra) [India], October 22: The Mindfulness India Summit 2024, an initiative by the Mindful Science Centre, presented by HSBC and supported by CII Leadership and HR Committee, successfully concluded its two-day event on October 17 and 18, 2024, establishing new benchmarks in corporate culture and personal well-being. With over 40 international and national experts addressing mindfulness, emotional intelligence, and neuroscience, the summit highlighted how these principles are essential in transforming leadership, enhancing employee engagement, and fostering sustainable well-being within organizations. The evolving workplace landscape, particularly the increasing role of AI, requires a renewed focus on human-centric leadership and emotional resilience. The summit provided a platform for forward-thinking leaders to explore how mindfulness can effectively bridge this gap, ensuring both corporate excellence and employee well-being . The summit featured MasterChef Sanjeev Kapoor as the Chief Guest, who shared how mindful leadership has played a pivotal role in building his culinary empire. Along with Chris Ruane, Ex MP British Parliament and Chair of Mindfulness Initiative UK, J N Behl and Global Holistic Health Guru Mickey Mehta, Kapoor also launched Manish Behl's new book "Observe - 101 Mindfulness Practices", a guide designed to make mindfulness accessible for both professionals and individuals in their everyday lives. Behl, a global mindfulness expert and founder of the Mindful Science Centre, shared, "With this book, I want to demystify mindfulness and make it accessible to everyone. Mindfulness is not a complex or distant concept, but a practical tool for reducing stress, improving focus, and fostering deeper connections in both personal and professional settings." The Mindfulness India Summit 2024 has successfully proven that mindfulness is no longer a luxury but a necessity in modern corporate structures. By adopting mindfulness practices, organizations are not only creating more compassionate work environments but are also enhancing their overall performance and sustainability in a world increasingly shaped by technological and emotional complexity. The 2 days also saw the launch of Mindfulness Impact Awards, to honor organizations and individuals who have integrated mindfulness into their corporate structures and personal lives. These awards reflect the growing recognition that workplace culture directly affects employee productivity, creativity, and overall well-being. Manish Behl, founder of the awards, explained, "Corporate success today goes beyond profit; it's about fostering environments where employees thrive mentally, emotionally, and physically. Our vision with these awards is to inspire a deeper integration of mindfulness in corporate cultures worldwide. By recognizing these pioneers, we hope these awards inspire companies and individuals to further integrate mindfulness into their environments, ultimately fostering happier, more productive workplaces, communities, and a more compassionate world." The awards were designed to acknowledge champions of mindfulness across categories, recognizing those who incorporate mindful practices to improve workplace culture, employee engagement, and societal impact. Winners ranged from corporate giants like Aditya Birla Group and Accenture to global educators and community leaders. items.title: "No shortage of oil in world and prices should hopefully come down", says Hardeep Singh Puri
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): Hardeep Singh Puri, Minister for Petroleum and Natural Gas on Tuesday said that there is no shortage of oil in the world and prices will come down soon, answering the question of the recent upswing in crude oil prices. Speaking to the media, the Union Minister cited global factors such as the war in the Middle East and voluntary cuts in oil production which are influencing the oil prices in the global market. He said, "It depends on global factors. One thing is very clear, there is no shortage of oil in the world...Today, more and more oil is coming on the market...There are other factors like geopolitical tensions. So, there is no shortage of oil but if there is tension in one part of the world, then the freight cost, and insurance freight cost will go up. Today, let us all hope that better sense prevails, that call for peace that our Prime Minister has been making from every forum...There is more than enough oil in the world and prices should hopefully come down. That's my expectation..." "If there's tension in one part of the world, then the cost of, if you have to take a longer route, then the cost of the freight cost, the insurance rate cost, that will go up...There's more than enough oil in the world, and prices should hopefully come down," he commented in his personal capacity.

The union minister said many countries such as Brazil, and Guayana among others are coming with their oil. Citing the stable prices in the last 3 years, the minister said that the government is taking every possible step to ensure stable oil prices. "Central government at every stage has stepped in to cushion and bring the prices down from November 2021 to May 2022. Now there are some global factors. The cost at the retail point is determined by the cost of the barrel in the international market plus the cost of transportation, freight, insurance, retailers, refining cost and margin, then dealers, margin, etc. We are solving all the problems we can, now you tell the global community to hold and bring them down," he added. This comes after oil prices rose nearly 2 per cent on Monday, reclaiming major losses from last week's sell-off. Brent crude features upped by $1.44, or 1.97 per cent in the afternoon. Earlier this month, Puri had said that the country is well-prepared to meet its growing energy demands, with a diverse range of oil sources. Speaking on the availability of oil in the global market, Puri emphasised that India has expanded its procurement base, moving from 27 suppliers to 39. (ANI)

items.title: Half of NASA's aging Mars fleet knocked offline by technical issues
paras: 115 million miles away Half of NASA’s aging Mars fleet knocked offline by technical issues Perseverance is having trouble transmitting to Earth. Odyssey is rapidly burning through its waning fuel supply.

19 ... ... ... NASA’s Perseverance looks down at a rocky outcrop nicknamed “Arathusa” in this selfie mosaic created using images taken from the vehicle's robotic arm. Credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech/MSSS NASA’s Perseverance looks down at a rocky outcrop nicknamed “Arathusa” in this selfie mosaic created using images taken from the vehicle's robotic arm. Credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech/MSSS Text settings Story text Size Small Standard Large Width * Standard Wide Links Standard Orange * Subscribers only Learn more Minimize to nav Two of NASA’s four missions operating at Mars have suspended science operations after encountering separate technical issues in recent weeks.

The missions affected by the outages — hopefully temporary — are NASA’s Perseverance rover and Odyssey orbiter. Both are operating beyond their original design lifetimes. Perseverance is in its sixth year exploring the surface of Mars, having collected rock and soil samples for eventual return to Earth. The rover is now studying the rim of a crater that once contained an ancient lake of liquid water. Odyssey arrived in orbit around Mars in 2001, and is the longest-lived Mars mission in history.

The problem on Perseverance stems from the rover’s communications system. The rover has two redundant UHF radios for high-rate communications with a fleet of orbiters that relay data to Earth. A separate X-band system is available for direct-to-Earth communications at a lower data rate.

One of the rover’s two UHF radios was unresponsive when it powered up on October 30, triggering an automatic switch to the backup radio and placing the rover in safe mode. Ground teams at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory in California later discovered the backup UHF radio was transmitting at about half of its expected power output, NASA said in a statement last week.
“The team has stopped using both radios until they can evaluate potential causes of the issues and one or both are deemed safe to resume operating,” NASA said.

Perseverance is now transmitting signals directly to Earth in X-band, but the connection provides a “significantly lower data rate” than relaying signals through orbiters using the UHF radios. Mission managers paused the rover’s science operations “out of an abundance of caution” as they investigate the radio problem. Their initial focus is on getting the backup UHF radio running before turning their attention on recovering the primary radio, NASA said.
“The team is hopeful the rover could return to science by the end of November.”

The six-wheeled robot broke a record last month for the farthest any vehicle has driven on another planet. The Perseverance rover surpassed the 28.06-mile (45.16-kilometer) mark set by NASA’s Opportunity rover, which stopped working in 2018. Perseverance’s odometer now sits at twice the rover’s original goal for distance traveled.

The situation with the Odyssey orbiter seems more dire. One of the four reaction wheels used for pointing the spacecraft stopped spinning in early November, leaving Odyssey with two good wheels after the first one failed in 2013. The orbiter needs at least three wheels to keep it oriented correctly.

“Without the three reaction wheels, the spacecraft must rely solely on its hydrazine thrusters to remain oriented,” NASA said. The orbiter requires stable pointing to turn its solar arrays toward the Sun and its science instruments toward Mars.

Odyssey was running low on propellant before the reaction wheel malfunction, but managers were optimistic that with “extremely low” fuel usage, the orbiter would have enough to continue operating through at least the end of 2028, said Jeffrey Plaut, Odyssey’s project scientist at JPL, in a presentation earlier this year.

That assumed no failures in Odyssey’s three remaining reaction wheels. Without three healthy wheels, engineers estimate the spacecraft has enough hydrazine fuel to last one to two months, NASA said. The good news is ground teams had some initial success troubleshooting the balky reaction wheel. Further testing is necessary to determine whether the wheel is recoverable.

Odyssey is one of four orbiters NASA uses to relay data between Earth and the Perseverance and Curiosity rovers on the Martian surface. Curiosity is still driving and collecting data after 14 years on Mars. The other three relay craft are NASA’s Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter, which reached the red planet in 2006, the European Space Agency’s 10-year-old ExoMars Trace Gas Orbiter, and ESA’s 23-year-old Mars Express spacecraft.

NASA lost contact with its MAVEN orbiter last December after 11 years of operations at Mars when the spacecraft suddenly spun out of control. An investigation could not identify a specific root cause, but engineers concluded that a radiation-induced single event upset or a software issue caused MAVEN’s flight computer to reboot, according to Tiffany Morgan, director of NASA’s robotic Mars Exploration Program.

The spacecraft’s inertial measurement unit failed to provide the computer with correct information on MAVEN’s orientation, causing it to spin in response to the faulty data, Morgan said in a November 9 presentation to the Mars Exploration Program Analysis Group.

NASA is preparing to send reinforcements to renew the agency’s presence at Mars. In September, NASA awarded Blue Origin a $700 million contract for the Mars Telecommunications Network (MTN), an orbiter dedicated to providing high-bandwidth connectivity between Earth and other missions operating on and around the red planet.

NASA wanted Blue Origin to complete the telecom orbiter by the end of 2028 and have it operational at Mars in 2030. But the Mars Telecommunications Network is on hold after Rocket Lab, which lost its bid to win the MTN contract, filed a protest with the Government Accountability Office . The GAO is expected to rule on the protest next month, at which time Blue Origin could start work on the NASA contract if the government rejects Rocket Lab’s petition.
Another Mars mission, SkyFall , could also launch in 2028. NASA aims to send three helicopter drones to Mars to explore the planet’s geology and weather from the air.

A perennial priority for Mars scientists is replacing the unique high-resolution mapping camera on the aging Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter. Such a capability will help identify landing sites for future robotic and human missions, including a potential mission to return Perseverance’s rock specimens to Earth.

NASA is in the very early stages of developing a mission concept that could take over MRO’s imaging capability, but there’s no firm schedule or budget for such an undertaking. NASA will likely rely on MRO for landing-site reconnaissance well into the 2030s.

items.title: Microsoft's historic cloud outage exposed an engineering “fog of war”
paras: Red Alert Microsoft’s historic cloud outage exposed an engineering “fog of war” Internal memos reveal a “Code Red” overhaul and ambitious one-hour recovery goals.

46 ... ... ... Credit: Microsoft Credit: Microsoft Text settings Story text Size Small Standard Large Width * Standard Wide Links Standard Orange * Subscribers only Learn more Minimize to nav According to internal memos reviewed by Reuters , Microsoft has declared a “Code Red” overhaul of its engineering response practices after the November 12 outage that lost access to Exchange Online, Teams, and Outlook for users worldwide.

Per the memos, Microsoft 365 Core President Jason Henderson described the outage as having the most customer impact in the history of Exchange Online. In a separate memo, Henderson wrote that an urgent production fix in a recent incident took five to six days to reach worldwide saturation. Microsoft’s target for its most urgent security fixes is to move from detection to safe worldwide deployment in one hour. “Needless to say, we aren’t here yet,” Henderson wrote.

The memos, which Reuters reviewed but Microsoft has not published, outline the response to the November 12 disruption. The company’s post-incident report , dated November 20, attributed the downtime to an undetected Windows scalability defect introduced in July, which caused lock contention in the gateway processes. A Teams traffic failover then dumped additional load onto infrastructure already under stress, as maintenance had left nearly 14 percent of gateway server capacity offline at the time of the incident.

Amanda Silver , a corporate vice president overseeing Microsoft 365 Core and Work IQ, wrote that engineers had to contend with a “fog of war” as the outage unfolded. According to Silver, responders exchanged more than 11,000 messages across 11 Teams chats, leaving diagnostic data scattered, and a full view of the incident fractured. Silver’s memo also quotes Charles Lamanna, executive vice president of Copilot, Agents and Platform, telling a Code Red review that the affected component had accumulated “roughly ten years’ worth of acceptable failures.”

Microsoft has said the outage was not related to any cyberattack or malicious activity, and the defects were not caused by AI tooling. As part of the Code Red overhaul, Silver’s memo outlines five workstreams focused on load shedding, geographic traffic partitioning, and faster recovery mechanisms. According to Reuters, Microsoft plans to improve its incident response and patching timelines by deploying its own AI agents to help engineers diagnose system health data more quickly. Henderson said that he will hold daily meetings with the Substrate leadership team, which oversees the engineering team responsible for Microsoft 365 services.

Microsoft has set targets of one-hour worldwide resolution in major incidents and a one-hour deployment window for urgent security fixes. It hasn’t said when it hopes to meet them, or how future response efforts will avoid 11 separate Teams chats and the “fog of war.”

items.title: November 25, 1999: The day Agassi was crowned year-end world No 1, two years after dropping out of the top 100
paras: On this day, November 25, 1999, Andre Agassi beat Gustavo Kuerten in straight sets to secure the year-end world No 1 ranking On this day, November 25, 1999, Andre Agassi defeated Gustavo Kuerten in the last round-robin match of the ATP Tour World Championships (6-4, 7-5).
Hard to believe, considering that only two years before, Agassi had dropped down to world No 141 before making his way back to the top. Andre Agassi, the Las Vegas Kid, was also a tennis legend.

After finishing runner-up three times, once at the 1990 US Open and twice at Roland-Garros (1990 and 1991), he claimed his first Grand Slam tournament at Wimbledon in 1992, defeating big serving Goran Ivanisevic in the final (6-7, 6-4, 6-4, 1-6, 6-4). This title was followed by the 1994 US Open and the 1995 Australian Open , the only time he beat his long-time rival, Pete Sampras, in a Grand Slam final (4-6, 6-1, 7-6, 6-4).

items.title: Andy Roddick spotted what was happening when Carlos Alcaraz was returning vs Alexander Zverev, ‘it gave me anxiety’
paras: Carlos Alcaraz has now won three consecutive matches against Alexander Zverev on the ATP circuit. Alcaraz extended his recent spell of dominance against the German by beating him in the ATP Finals final on Sunday.

The Spaniard, who triumphed 6-2, 7-6 inside the Inalpi Arena, has now won 30 ATP titles; equalling Jannik Sinner’s career total. Andy Roddick was left particularly impressed by Alcaraz , claiming that one area of the 23-year-old’s game made him feel anxious.

“The thing that Carlos was turning into in real time with his returns [against Zverev] was like Novak,” Roddick claimed on the Served Podcast. “Novak was simultaneously the best aggressive returner when he needed to be and also the best aggressive returner when he needed to be. Where does Carlos Alcaraz now rank among the best players in tennis history?

items.title: Jimmy Connors issues warning to Aryna Sabalenka after her difficult 2026 season
paras: Aryna Sabalenka failed to win a Grand Slam and lost her world number-one ranking in 2026. She enjoyed a strong start to the year, winning the Brisbane International and reaching the Australian Open final, before completing the Sunshine Double, but has struggled for form ever since.

Sabalenka finishes 2026 as the world number three, her lowest year-end ranking in four years (5th in 2022). Tennis legend Jimmy Connors has now delivered his verdict on Sabalenka’s 2026 WTA Tour campaign.

Because once you are not winning anymore, and you are not selling out 25,000-seat stadiums, you know what the one word you have to get used to is? I hate to say it like that, but it’s true. Look at this 19-year-old [Mirra Andreeva]; she is coming. If Sabalenka can’t do it, they are going to hook on to her because she will sell out the stadiums.

items.title: Meet the player who won 36 consecutive matches at the Davis Cup and beat Bjorn Borg’s all-time record
paras: The 11-time Grand Slam champion compiled a 37-3 singles record at the international team event, winning 33 consecutive singles rubbers between 1973 and 1980. During the run, Borg led Sweden to their one and only Davis Cup title .

Around 46 years after Borg’s final Davis Cup match, his record of 33 straight match wins was eclipsed. Marcos Baghdatis, a finalist at the 2006 Australian Open, won his 34th consecutive Davis Cup singles rubber on March 4, 2017.

The Cypriot star secured the record after defeating Andorran player Jean-Baptiste Poux-Gautier in Europe Zone Group III in Estonia. Baghdatis went on to win 36 consecutive matches before losing to Tunisian world number 799 Moez Echargui, 5-7, 6-7, 6-4, 6-4, 1-6. The Cypriot’s run ran from 2003 to 2017. Ten years earlier, Baghdatis stated his desire to win the Davis Cup for Cyprus.

Friendships are built by repeated contact, not by being liked
items.hook: This is the single most useful fact in the whole guide.
paras: Studies of primary-school classrooms found that children seated next to each other were far more likely to become friends than children seated across the room. When teachers changed the seating, new friendships formed with the new neighbours.

So the engine is: same place, same people, same activity, over and over. The day at the yo-yo bar followed by basketball is that engine working - shared activity changed how the other boy treated him. It was not luck.
items.do: Pick one activity he already likes and commit to it weekly for a full term.

items.title: Keep the proximity - change the watching
items.hook: Your instinct is half right, and the other half matters.
paras: You are right that being around the group matters: children nominate as friends the children they see and interact with most. 'Out of sight, out of mind' is real for acquaintances.

But guidance written for schools is blunt: merely remaining beside a group is not friendship. A child who hovers is read as a bystander rather than a player, and it holds him in the one-down position. Watching has a use - but only as the first twenty seconds of joining in, never as the endpoint.
items.do: Keep telling him to stay near the group. Add: 'then take a job in the game'.

items.title: Teach 'watch, then blend'
items.hook: The best way to join a game is not to ask.
paras: Most of us were told to walk up and say 'Can I play?' But that makes everyone stop and look at him, and makes 'no' very easy.

The better sequence, used by people who study play: watch for about twenty seconds to learn the game and where the line is, then slide into the action without stopping it. Take the end of the line. Stand in the outfield. Pick up the ball and pass it back.
items.do: Rehearse it at home in five minutes. Ask him to name the 'easiest job' in each game.

items.title: Host one friend at a time - this is the biggest lever you control
items.hook: The child who invites is rarely short of friends.
paras: Pick a child he has had fun with in the last month, not someone he admires from afar. Invite one person for one to two hours. Put away anything precious, have two activities ready, start with a snack, and let the guest choose sometimes.
Keep it short and end while they are both still enjoying it. Then leave a few weeks before inviting the same child again, so the invitation can come back to him.
items.do: Text one parent this week and set a date for the school holidays.

items.title: Ask the teacher one specific question
items.hook: Teachers see the playground. Ask them to name names.
paras: Ask two things: who does he play well with, and could he be seated near them or paired with them for group work?
Seating is one of the few levers that reliably creates new friendships, and it is invisible to the children - no one has to know it was arranged.
items.do: Email the teacher this week with those two questions.

items.title: Do not push into a group that is rejecting him
items.hook: Here the advice is the opposite of persistence.
paras: Where a group is actively excluding him, the guidance is to back off - when you back off from people, they can move towards you. Put his energy into two or three other children instead of one closed circle.
Friends in more than one place - school, a club, family friends - also make him far less vulnerable when one group turns cold.
items.do: Help him list three children outside the difficult group he could get to know.

items.title: One or two good friends is the goal - not popularity
paras: Kids need one or two good friends. You do not need to worry about him being the most popular child in the class.
His warmth and kindness are already the raw material. Treat this as coaching a skill, not fixing a fault - if he feels like a project, he will resist.
items.do: Say his strengths out loud, often. Confidence is what carries a child into a group.

items.title: Playing and talking with girls is normal and good
items.hook: Children believe gender matters far more than it actually does.
paras: In one large classroom experiment, simply seating boys and girls next to each other doubled how often they became friends.
Girls' play tends to build conversation, turn-taking and inventing games together; boys' play builds bigger, faster group play. Being good at both widens his circle.
items.do: No action needed. Just do not let him think it is odd.

items.title: When to get more help
items.hook: Ordinary friendship difficulty is not a disorder.
paras: Get more support if he becomes reluctant to go to school, is persistently distressed, has changes in sleep or appetite, or says it is happening all the time and he cannot make it stop.
Start with his teacher, then the school counsellor, then your GP for a referral. Kids Helpline is free and open 24/7 on 1800 55 1800, for children and for parents.
items.do: Save Kids Helpline in your phone: 1800 55 1800.
